subject.title: [Feature]:  Missing Session Management Commands in OpenClaw

question: What public session lifecycle contract should OpenClaw expose for stop, kill, pause, resume, and resource limits across Gateway, CLI, and UI?
rationale: Current main has partial abort/delete/reset/cleanup primitives, but the requested controls affect authorization, child-process ownership, persisted session state, UI wording, and possible config defaults, so automation cannot safely choose the product boundary.

options.title: Design Additive Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Add explicit guarded Gateway methods plus CLI/UI affordances for stop, kill, pause, resume, and resource policy while preserving current abort/delete defaults and documenting upgrade behavior.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Canonical Work
options.body: Keep this umbrella open and route child-process kill, topic UI, resume/fork, and diagnostics to their narrower related issues before deciding a broad API.

options.title: Defer Broad Controls
options.body: Keep current abort/delete/cleanup behavior and document limitations until resource and process lifecycle ownership is designed.

recommendation.title: Design Additive Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Add explicit guarded Gateway methods plus CLI/UI affordances for stop, kill, pause, resume, and resource policy while preserving current abort/delete defaults and documenting upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current-main history across the Gateway, CLI, UI, and session lifecycle surfaces this decision would touch.
